transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

My sleep has been completely off for weeks—either I’m up most of the night with my mind going or I crash and still wake up feeling worn out. It's gotten to the point where I just can't keep going like this.
Apart from your sleep issues, have you been experiencing persistent feelings of sadness, or a loss of interest in activities you normally enjoy?

Yes, when my energy drops, a heavy gray cloud settles over me and I feel so useless and guilty about letting my family down. I've also completely lost interest in things I used to love, like knitting, volunteering at the food pantry, and going to church—it all just feels pointless now.
You mentioned your mind is often racing at night. Do you find yourself constantly worrying about many different everyday things, and is this worry difficult to control?

Yes, my mind is constantly running like a motor at night and I just can't seem to control it. My thoughts race from one thing to another—like doctor bills, my mom's health, and work tasks—piling on so fast that I can't grab hold of any single one of them.
How long have you been experiencing this constant, hard-to-control worry about everyday things? Has it been going on for at least six months, or did it start more recently with your mood changes?
No, it hasn't been six months at all. It started much more recently, about three months ago, right around the time my daughter had to move back in and my mother's health really started to slide.
Have these feelings of sadness, low energy, and loss of interest been present nearly every day, for most of the day, for at least the past two weeks?

Yes, those heavy, sad feelings and not caring about anything have been there nearly every single day, for most of the day. It's actually been going on much longer than two weeks—it's been about three months now, ever since my daughter's divorce and my mom's health started sliding. I just feel so completely worn down and overwhelmed by it all.
During this difficult time, have you had any thoughts of death, or felt that you would be better off dead?

Yes, there have been moments, especially after a bad argument at home or when I mess up at work, where I catch myself thinking it might be easier if I just didn't wake up. I get to feeling like my family would be better off without me dragging everyone down. I want to be clear that I haven't made any plans to actually hurt myself, but those thoughts do cross my mind when things get really low.

Have you ever experienced periods of time lasting several days where you felt the exact opposite of depressed—such as having unusually high energy, needing very little sleep, or feeling on top of the world?

Yes, I definitely have those "up" periods, which have been happening on and off for about three months now. During those times, I feel on top of the world and convinced I can handle everything, but I also get so irritable that I snap at everyone while tearing around starting multiple projects. I can easily get by on just three or four hours of sleep and still feel completely wired the next day.
When you experience these 'up' periods of high energy and needing very little sleep, how many days in a row do they typically last?

I'm not entirely sure of the exact number of days because I tend to lose track of time when I'm in that wired state. But it definitely feels like those high-energy spells last for several days at a time before I finally crash.
During these high-energy periods, have you ever experienced severe problems at work or home, or have you ever needed to be hospitalized because of them?

I haven't been hospitalized, but I've definitely had severe problems at work and at home. I was recently written up at the warehouse for making mistakes and missing shifts, and at home, my family is constantly tiptoeing around me because they don't know what to expect. They've even started taking over responsibilities I used to handle because of how unpredictable I've been.
During these high-energy periods, do you find yourself doing things that are risky or unusual for you, such as spending too much money, driving recklessly, or making impulsive decisions?

I haven't really done specific things like driving recklessly or spending too much money. But I do get very carried away with starting a million projects at once and taking on too many tasks, like tearing around the house reorganizing everything.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling consistently depressed and low, or have you been experiencing a rapid mix of both high-energy and low-mood states happening at the same time?

I don't really feel them at the exact same time, but rather I swing back and forth between the two. I'll go from being in a high-energy, wired overdrive where I feel on top of the world and take on everything, to suddenly crashing into a heavy gray cloud where I feel useless, guilty, and completely exhausted. These unpredictable ups and downs have been going on like this for about three months now.

During the periods when you feel depressed and down, how much does it affect your ability to do daily activities like work, chores, or taking care of yourself—is it very difficult but you still manage, or has it become almost impossible to do anything?

It has become incredibly difficult, almost impossible at times when that heavy gray cloud is over me. I've been written up at the warehouse for mistakes and missed shifts, and I've completely stopped showing up to church or volunteering. At home, my family has had to start taking over tasks I used to manage because I just can't keep up anymore.

When you swing between these high-energy and low-mood states, how quickly do these shifts happen? Do you switch back and forth within a few days or even hours, or does each state last for several weeks?

These shifts have been happening back and forth over the last three months. It really varies—some days I feel incredibly wound up and on top of the world, while other days I crash into that heavy, useless feeling, rather than staying in one state for weeks on end without change.
Over the past two weeks, have you been in a constant, unbroken state of deep depression, or have you continued to rapidly swing back and forth between high-energy and low-energy states?

No, I haven't been in a constant state of depression; I'm still swinging back and forth between those wired states and the heavy crashes. These intense ups and downs have been going on for about three months now. It's just incredibly exhausting to flip from feeling on top of the world and restless to suddenly sinking into that heavy, guilty low.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with rapid alternation between manic/hypomanic symptoms (unusually high energy, decreased need for sleep, extreme irritability, racing thoughts, and increased goal-directed activity) and depressive symptoms (persistent depressed mood, anhedonia, fatigue, feelings of worthlessness, and passive suicidal ideation) over the past three months. This rapid switching between poles rather than a sustained single-polarity episode satisfies the criteria for Bipolar affective disorder, current episode mixed (F31.6).
